essay:
The percentage of overweight children in Western society has increased significantly over the last decade, becoming a major public health concern. This essay will discuss the main causes of this disturbing trend and its effects on children and society.

One of the primary causes is the busy lifestyle of parents. Many parents work long hours and have little time to prepare healthy meals at home. As a result, children often rely on fast food or ready-to-eat meals, which are usually high in calories and low in nutrients. Another important factor is the influence of social media and food delivery applications such as SkipTheDishes and Uber Eats. These companies advertise heavily through influencers, short videos, and attractive promotions, encouraging children to choose unhealthy food instead of nutritious meals. For example, a study conducted by the University of British Columbia in 2020 found that children exposed to influencer advertisements were more likely to prefer fast food.

This trend has several negative consequences. Firstly, consuming excessive amounts of junk food can lead to obesity, poor physical development, and health problems because these foods contain high levels of unhealthy fats, sugar, and salt while providing fewer essential vitamins and minerals. Secondly, the increasing use of food delivery services creates more plastic packaging waste, much of which is non-recyclable. This contributes to environmental pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. Finally, regularly purchasing fast food can place a financial burden on families because these meals are often more expensive than home-cooked food.

In conclusion, the rise in childhood obesity is mainly caused by parents' busy work schedules and the strong influence of social media advertising. Unless healthier eating habits are encouraged at home and unhealthy food marketing is better controlled, this problem is likely to continue growing.
